theory.overview: A Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) is a subset of edges that connects all vertices in a weighted, undirected graph with the minimum total edge weight. MSTs have exactly V-1 edges (no cycles). Two classic algorithms solve this: Kruskal's (sorts edges, uses union-find, O(E log E)) and Prim's (grows tree from a node, uses priority queue, O(E log V)). MSTs have applications in network design, clustering, and approximation algorithms.

keyConcepts.name: Kruskal's Algorithm
keyConcepts.description: Sort all edges by weight. Add edges in order, skipping those that form cycles (detected with Union-Find). Greedy approach.

keyConcepts.name: Prim's Algorithm
keyConcepts.description: Start from arbitrary node. Grow tree by adding cheapest edge connecting tree to non-tree vertex. Like Dijkstra but with edge weights.

keyConcepts.name: Cut Property
keyConcepts.description: For any cut of the graph, the minimum weight edge crossing the cut belongs to some MST. Foundation of MST algorithms.

keyConcepts.name: Union-Find (Disjoint Set)
keyConcepts.description: Data structure for Kruskal's. Supports union (connect sets) and find (which set) in nearly O(1) with path compression.

complexity.kruskal: O(E log E) - dominated by sorting
complexity.prim: O(E log V) with binary heap

algorithmSteps.description: Kruskal's: Start with sorted edges, empty MST. Each node is its own component.
Sort all edges by weight ascending: (C-D,1), (B-C,2), (B-D,3), (A-B,4), (A-D,5)
Add C-D (weight 1): C and D in different components. Include in MST. 3 components remain.
Add B-C (weight 2): B and C-D in different components. Include. 2 components remain.
Skip B-D (weight 3): B and D already in same component! Would form cycle.
Add A-B (weight 4): A connects to B-C-D component. Include. 1 component - MST complete!
MST complete with 3 edges, total weight = 1+2+4 = 7. All 4 nodes connected.
